result.title: We Ran a Research Sprint With AI. The AI Worked. The Research Didn't
result.summary: Generative AI tools for research are widely deployed, yet individual productivity gains do not guarantee better team research. We argue that how AI use is structured matters alongside access. Personal AI tools may amplify two failures under deadline pressure: a consumption bottleneck, in which generation outpaces team-visible evaluation, and AI-induced research silos, in which private human-AI loops displace shared decision-making. We motivate this position with a mechanism-generating pilot: a 100-minute research sprint with twelve researchers in three independently operating teams, within a seventeen-person session. Both patterns recurred across teams and evidence sources. Of 33 logged AI interactions, one was accepted outright and 27 lacked a recorded disposition; missing records alone do not establish absent evaluation. A parallel autonomous pipeline produced a complete draft without in-session human evaluation, illustrating production capacity rather than comparative quality. We propose Human-AI-Human collaboration: an interaction topology in which AI connects researchers' contexts and supports inspectable collective evaluation and decision-making. The pilot does not isolate AI-specific effects from time pressure or workflow practices. We close with seven modular, falsifiable design hypotheses, prioritizing shared context and team-visible evaluation checkpoints for controlled follow-up.

AI.brief_summary: 该文是一篇立场/观点论文，基于一次 100 分钟、12 名研究者的科研冲刺观察，论证个人式 AI 工具会造成「生成快于团队可评估」的消费瓶颈与人机私有回路造成的协作孤岛，并提出 Human-AI-Human 协作拓扑与七条可检验设计假设。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究对象是人类团队的科研协作流程与 AI 使用结构，不涉及多模态推理的表示、latent 状态生成或视觉证据使用，其评估与验证讨论停留在团队工作流层面，与 LVR 无具体可迁移线索。
